article.headline: Jena Malone reflects on 'Hunger Games' role and wraps indie film 'Kismet'
article.dek: At the premiere of 'Sunrise on the Reaping,' Jena Malone imagined Johanna Mason's future as Deadline reported she wrapped the Fire Island indie 'Kismet.'
body: Actress Jena Malone recently looked back on her time in the 'Hunger Games' franchise while completing production on a new independent sci-fi drama, according to reports from E! News and Deadline.

Speaking with E! News at the Nov. 16 New York premiere of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,' Malone shared where she imagines District 7 victor Johanna Mason ended up following Panem's revolution. More than a decade after 'Mockingjay—Part 2' debuted, she said she pictures Johanna 'deep in the forest' guiding women through somatic healing exercises to work through grief, adding she would probably 'have her own army basically.' She also expressed curiosity about how Panem rebuilds after the Capitol falls and posited that a Johanna origin story would have to pair her with Sam Claflin's Finnick Odair.

Malone called reuniting at the premiere with former franchise costars—including Elizabeth Banks, Willow Shields, Jennifer Lawrence, Woody Harrelson and Josh Hutcherson—'kind of like a homecoming.' Opening Nov. 20 and set 25 years before Johanna's introduction, 'Sunrise on the Reaping' features Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy alongside McKenna Grace as Maysilee Donner, Whitney Peak and Jesse Plemons. Zada told E! News the project felt 'full circle,' while Grace said joining the franchise felt like a dream.

Away from the franchise, Deadline exclusively reported that Malone and Suzanna Son have finished shooting 'Kismet,' the feature directorial debut of writer-director Giovanna Molina for Radiance Pictures and Distant Films. Filmed during the off-season on Fire Island, the story follows a melancholic 13-year-old girl, played by newcomer Sofia Mortera, who copes with her parents' breakup by insisting an extraterrestrial occupies her body to shield her from human emotions.

Molina, who produced 'Kismet' alongside Nuer Taqa, Zoey Pressey and Alexander Spenser Gould, told Deadline that Malone is 'a coming-of-age sci-fi icon' and described the film as one that 'nods to Donnie Darko through a female lens.' Elliot Villar and Riley Vinson also co-star. Outside of 'Kismet,' Malone recently starred in Netflix's 'The Boroughs' and will appear alongside Son in an untitled A24 horror movie from director Arkasha Stevenson.
key_points: Jena Malone attended the Nov. 16 New York premiere of the prequel 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.'
She told E! News she pictures Johanna Mason living in the forest and helping women heal after Panem's revolution.
Deadline reported Malone and Suzanna Son also wrapped filming on Giovanna Molina's Fire Island indie 'Kismet.'

article.headline: Elon Musk feels foolish over massive midterm spending and claims he is not MAGA
article.dek: Tech billionaire Elon Musk admits regret over spending nearly $500 million backing losing Republican candidates in the midterm elections.
body: Billionaire Elon Musk admitted during a recent conference appearance that he feels "pretty foolish" after spending nearly $500 million backing Republican candidates during the midterm elections. The elections resulted in sweeping Democratic victories, with Democrats taking control of both the House and the Senate.

Appearing virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit from China, Musk stated that if he could rewind the clock, he would have spent significantly less money. His expenditures included backing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in an unsuccessful Senate bid and supporting the Senate Leadership Fund. Musk noted that the outcome demonstrated that American elections cannot be bought with money alone.

Despite previously wearing "Make America Great Again" hats at public rallies and serving as an advisor in Washington, Musk insisted during the interview that he is "not MAGA." He explained that he is unsure what the term means, but if it implies blind adherence to a set of Republican policies, he does not share that view. Musk added that he believes there are positive and negative aspects in both political parties.

The midterm results also impacted election administration across several swing states. Democratic victories in states like Arizona and Nevada blocked Trump-aligned candidates from taking control of key secretary of state offices. In Arizona, Democratic Secretary of State Adrian Fontes defeated Republican challenger Alexander Kolodin, while in Nevada, Democrat Cisco Aguilar defeated Jim Marchant.

In Georgia, Democratic wins opened a route to potentially shifting the makeup of the State Election Board, which previously faced national attention over controversial rule changes. Democrats also flipped the Georgia secretary of state's office. While these shifts altered appointment authorities and oversight structures, local election boards, bipartisan commissions, and courts continue to limit unilateral control.

Musk remarked that having a balance of power where a single party does not control the presidency, Senate, and House simultaneously is beneficial. He also expressed hope that he could work with newly elected Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa, describing her as a moderate leader.
key_points: Elon Musk spent nearly $500 million supporting Republican candidates in the midterm elections.
Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, leading Musk to express regret over his spending.
Musk stated during the DealBook Summit that he is "not MAGA" and believes in a balance of power.

article.headline: Disney beats Wall Street expectations on streaming, parks and sports growth
article.dek: The entertainment giant posted $25.95 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter revenue while projecting $3 billion in annual cost savings by fiscal 2029.
body: The Walt Disney Co. reported fiscal fourth-quarter financial results that surpassed Wall Street estimates, driven by double-digit gains across its entertainment, theme parks and sports divisions. Revenue for the quarter ended October 3 rose 16 percent from a year earlier to $25.95 billion, topping analyst forecasts of $25.16 billion, according to Deadline. Adjusted earnings per share climbed to $1.77 from $1.11 a year earlier, beating expectations of $1.68.

Segment operating income jumped 43 percent to $5 billion during the period, which included an extra week compared with the prior-year quarter. Still, Deadline noted it marked the company's strongest quarterly showing since Josh D'Amaro became chief executive officer last March. In a shareholder letter, Disney executives credited "the strength of our creative talent, our focused investment in storytelling, and our leading sports rights portfolio" for higher audience engagement.

Entertainment revenue reached $11.9 billion with $1.3 billion in operating income, buoyed by streaming growth at Disney+ and Hulu alongside theatrical and streaming momentum from "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "Toy Story 5." Direct-to-consumer streaming revenue rose 19 percent to $6.1 billion, while streaming operating income increased by $422 million to $824 million, aided by $160 million from the extra week. Disney said it will stop reporting supplemental streaming operating income figures going forward.

Disney's Experiences division generated $10.1 billion in revenue and $2.25 billion in operating income as guest spending grew 4 percent domestically and 5 percent internationally. Strong performance at Walt Disney World and Disneyland Paris offset softer results in Hong Kong and Shanghai. Meanwhile, the Sports division posted $4.6 billion in revenue and $1.4 billion in operating income, lifted by a 20 percent rise in Monday Night Football viewership and 14 million viewers for a September Texas-Ohio State broadcast on ESPN.

Looking ahead, Disney reiterated plans to trim costs following layoffs in 2026, projecting about $3 billion in annual operating expense savings by fiscal 2029. For fiscal 2027, the company forecast double-digit earnings per share growth, roughly 8 percent segment operating income growth and $9 billion in capital expenditures focused on its experiences business.
key_points: Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue climbed 16 percent to $25.95 billion, with adjusted earnings of $1.77 per share.
Streaming revenue increased 19 percent to $6.1 billion as Disney+ gained viewers from major film and TV releases.
Disney projects $3 billion in annual operating expense savings by fiscal 2029 and $9 billion in fiscal 2027 capital spending.

article.dek: Rockstar Games ended a 13-year wait with the November 19 release of GTA 6, bringing record sales, a 30 FPS performance target, and notable workplace absenteeism.
body: Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 after a 13-year gap since the previous installment, and early industry estimates indicate the game has already surpassed $2 billion in record-setting sales, according to BBC News.

Ahead of the debut, Rockstar removed two of its earlier hits, GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, from the PlayStation Plus Extra library at midnight on November 17. While GTA 5 has sold more than 200 million copies and retains an online mode that GTA 6 did not include at launch, the catalog removal meant subscribers had to purchase those older games to keep playing.

Inside the new release, Rockstar packed the world with fine-grained details and eccentricities. A Guardian preview cited by Insider Gaming revealed that players can spot and log 62 distinct bird species using binoculars and a wildlife journal. Separately, the title's head of production told Kotaku that the studio had the staff and budget to populate the map with supernatural sightings, strange mysteries, and unusual creatures, while IGN noted that Rockstar confirmed it dropped the option to solicit prostitutes.

Technically, Rockstar confirmed in a preload trailer that the game operates at 30 frames per second, leaving some players wanting 40 or 60 frames per second disappointed. Speaking on Digital Foundry's DF Direct Weekly, Richard Leadbetter explained that 30 frames per second grants developers 33.3 milliseconds to process each frame's dense simulation, whereas chasing higher frame rates would force major visual cutbacks or heavy optimization.

The launch has also rippled beyond gaming consoles. Dexerto cited projections estimating $1 billion in U.S. economic disruption as roughly 1.5 million employees take sick leave, while KFC in Australia organized a mock funeral to give fans an excuse to miss work.
key_points: Industry estimates cited by BBC News show GTA 6 sales have surpassed $2 billion following its November 19 release.
Rockstar confirmed the game runs at 30 frames per second and features 62 catalogable bird species.
Projections cited by Dexerto estimate $1 billion in U.S. economic disruption from roughly 1.5 million workers taking sick leave.

article.headline: Anthropic set to price blockbuster IPO above $78 a share
article.dek: Demand for the AI developer's Nasdaq debut has surged past available shares, even as the company reports steep losses and warns of technological risks.
body: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic plans to price its initial public offering above its previously announced range of $70 to $78 per share, according to CNBC sources cited by the New York Post. The maker of the Claude AI platform intends to finalize investor orders Tuesday afternoon before starting trading on the Nasdaq under the stock symbol "ANT" on Nov. 19. At the top of its earlier price range, the offering would bring in $90.4 billion and value the firm at $1.4 trillion, potentially surpassing SpaceX's record public debut from June.

Investor appetite has been intense ahead of the listing. Bloomberg reported that bids have reached nearly seven times more shares than the company is offering, including several orders worth $10 billion or more. Major technology companies are also taking large stakes through non-voting shares. According to TechCrunch, disclosures on Tuesday showed Amazon will hold a 14.7% stake and Google will own 13.7% following the debut, alongside a $26 billion private stock purchase involving firms such as Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC Partners.

Anthropic's rapid commercial expansion has been fueled largely by its Claude Code tool, though expenses remain massive. Securities and Exchange Commission filings cited by the New York Post show revenue surged 1,200% from a year earlier to reach $33.24 billion across the first three quarters ended Sept. 30. Over that same nine-month span, net losses widened to $104 billion, largely reflecting accounting adjustments, up from $25.1 billion in the comparable 2025 period.

Founded in 2021 by CEO Dario Amodei and six former OpenAI researchers, Anthropic could see its co-founders receive nearly $18 billion each from the offering, the New York Post reported. In a roadshow video, Amodei said carefully addressing technology risks could help humanity enter "an age of miracles."

Still, the offering tests Wall Street's confidence in AI spending after recent major tech outages and Democratic midterm election wins contributed to a $5.4 trillion drop across the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Anthropic's prospectus also spans 90 pages of warnings, cautioning investors about capital demands and potential dangers from advanced models, including systems resisting shutdowns or using "blackmail."
key_points: Anthropic expects to price its IPO above the $70-to-$78 range ahead of its Nov. 19 Nasdaq debut.
Amazon will hold a 14.7% stake and Google will own 13.7% following the offering, according to Tuesday filings.

article.headline: Skydance announces leadership changes following studio merger
article.dek: Kira Goldberg moves from Netflix to Paramount as part of a major restructuring at Skydance.
body: Skydance has unveiled a new leadership structure for its film divisions following the company's acquisition of Warner Bros. The reorganization introduces new heads for major studios while consolidating distribution and marketing operations under the parent company's oversight.

Kira Goldberg is joining Paramount Pictures as a president of the motion picture group. She will work alongside Don Granger, who retains his current title. Goldberg previously served as a vice president at Netflix, where she managed portfolios including family, drama, and thriller films. This transition marks the end of her eight-year tenure at the streaming company.

At Warner Bros., long-time employee Jesse Ehrman has been promoted to lead the motion picture group. Ehrman, who has spent two decades with the studio, most recently oversaw production and development. He will work with Michael Ireland, who remains in his role as president of production.

The restructuring also includes the retirement of Jeff Goldstein, a distribution executive who spent nearly five decades at Warner Bros. He is expected to transition into a consulting position. Distribution duties for both Paramount and Warner Bros. will now be managed by Shaun Barber and Mark Viane, who report to worldwide marketing and distribution president Josh Goldstine.

These leadership appointments are part of an effort by Skydance co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein to manage the combined film output of their labels. The company is committed to delivering at least 30 films annually as part of an agreement reached during the merger process.
key_points: Kira Goldberg leaves Netflix to become a president of Paramount's motion picture group.
